fixed.item: Performance (P1 gate G7: 3.85 vs ADOPT 3.21 ms per substep; climate.house 0.585 -> 0.625 ms in the gate records, +0.040): the increase was entirely the first substep of every episode, where the eight indexes model.scan / _scan_static look up on every substep were first built through the kernel's read views (review M3: an index built mid-step evaluates every entity through a _StartView / _ReadView).
fixed.how: common.index_reads declares every field a static-index predicate can read (World.static_index reads=; strict mode checks it), on every climate index predicate (the former lambdas are now named: common.has_kind, is_window, connects_rooms, combustible_candidate; model._gain_candidate, _power_candidate, _cover_candidate, _glare_candidate, _shade_candidate, _shower_candidate; fans._light_or_flame; sun._caster_candidate, _window_cover_candidate; moisture._settle_candidate, _floor_candidate, _mist_candidate). common.per_step_index registers the eight looked up every substep (common.PER_STEP: climate.windows, kinds, gains, showers, power, glare, shade_watch, cover) and an episode_start hook (order -90, before any hook that writes) builds them while nothing is journaled, so the World evaluates them on the plain records. The index content is a pure function of the state (World.static_index contract), so nothing computed changes. Exact steady-state trims in model.py / common.py: the air pass joins rooms into open-door zones only when a window is open (cross ventilation and window fans, which need an open window, are their only readers), _effects_step reads a window's facing only when it is open, window_open_area's opening shares are a module constant (WINDOW_PORTION) instead of a dict literal per call, _people_comfort lists the house's fans once per substep instead of once per person.
